body.x: Huvitech (CEO Seung-Ik Lee, www.huvitech.com) unveiled its 2-channel FULL HD black box and 4-channel rear view camera for automobiles at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The black box B7FHD is a dual channel black box capable of recording video in 1280 x 720p with a maximum definition of 1980 x 1080p. The black box has a 2 million pixel camera to record crystal clear videos in high definition.

The slim 3” LCD screen is foldable for better front view. Video recordings can instantly be viewed through the LCD monitor, and is built with a 3G shock sensor to detect and record any events that involve movements. Recording can be done in both continuous and emergency mode while its own viewer program allows the user to examine the device’s data in detail on a PC. The micro SD card from the black box can be inserted into most smartphones to playback the videos as well.

The D15 rearview system contains a 4-channel HD-DVR G-sensor and supports the H.264 codec. It is compatible with both SD and SSD and can automatically overwrite data on HDD. The G-Sensor allows the device to record in both a continuous and event modes as well as in parking mode. It has a 1.5 million pixel HD camera, wi-fi enabled, and the video can be checked through a smartphone application.

Huvitech has focused on the visual communication system and industry for many years and supplies a wide variety of products including rear view cameras, DVR systems, security systems, medical systems, and more. It continues to make significant investments into R&D to continuously develop high quality products for the global market.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
